name: AKU donates equipment to facilitate research and training in Mombasa County

content.title: AKU donates equipment to facilitate research and training in Mombasa County
content.summary: AKU study has provided supplies for the setup of two e-Resource centres in Mombasa county

media.caption: Prof Marleen Temmerman (right) hands over list of donated equipment to Dr Swabah Ahmed (left)
media.alt: AKU donates equipment to facilitate research and training in Mombasa County

content.text: Mombasa County's Department of Health Services received desktops, conference speakers, webcams, television sets, internet connectivity, and backup systems valued at approximately KES 600,000 from the Aga Khan University Centre of Excellence in Women and Child Health, East Africa (CoEWCH EA).
The supplies were a donation courtesy of the
Women in Health and their Economic, Equity and Livelihood statuses during Emergency Preparedness and Response (WHEELER)
project with funding from the Canadian International Development Research Centre (IDRC). The project is a collaboration between CoEWCH, EA, University of Manitoba, and Kilifi and Mombasa counties.

The materials will go towards the setting up of two e-Resource centres in Mombasa County that will be used to remotely connect the research team with both health care workers and community health promoters during the study and beyond. The e-Resource centres will facilitate capacity building of health care workers and community health promoters on research methods, gender related studies and other clinical courses delivered by the Aga Khan University and the University of Manitoba. By having these centres, the study will have facilitated diffusion of knowledge to health care workers who may not necessarily participate in on-site trainings.

"The equipment will make it easier for the teams to communicate and conduct the training from wherever they are as opposed to going to each site. This will save on time and money by connecting everyone and facilitating the research," said Prof Marleen Temmerman, Director, CoEWCH EA.

The WHEELER study aims to provide evidence on the effects and possible impact of work-related health and safety changes and the disruption to female paid and unpaid healthcare providers' (HCPs), economic opportunities and livelihood during the COVID-19 pandemic. This will be achieved by comparing how both male and female HCPs were affected to see if there were any differences in the impact. The study will use participatory and gender-based analysis approaches in generating the evidence to formulate gender inclusive and transformative strategies that will safeguard the female HCPs in the current pandemic and during emergency preparedness, response, and recovery phases in future health crises.

Mombasa's County Executive for the Department of Health Services, Dr Swabah Ahmed, commended the initiative by noting the importance of research in preparing for future emergencies. While extending support to the project, she encouraged the incorporation of capacity building to enhance research efforts and meet research needs in Mombasa County.

"We will closely follow the research to ensure that we curb the limitations the study might face. There also is readily available data that the study can use. I hope that this project will mentor others in research and look forward to future collaborations in health research with the Aga Khan University," she said.

The WHEELER study, in line with CoEWCH EA's mandate, is keen on building research capacity for young leaders. The project will mentor a master's student from the Technical University of Mombasa to fulfil this objective. The findings from the study will advise policy formulation to the two county governments that is specific and gender-responsive with the purpose of mitigating the negative effects that may result from emergencies such that livelihoods are not greatly disrupted.

"We hope that through this study we will be able to strengthen the research capacity within the public health system in addition to supporting the health system in generation of evidence-based gender responsive policy options for safeguarding the health care work force across all the levels during periods of crises," said Evaline Lang'at the study's principal investigator at CoEWCH, EA.
